# Survival supervision of the loadings (October 2026, in progress)

## Executive summary {.unnumbered}

1. **Test bed.** A planted prognostic program that explains 0.27% (noise multiplier 0.25) or
   0.02% (noise 1) of expression variance, alongside two non-prognostic programs that carry the
   variance. Fit at K = 7; 20 seeds per noise level.
2. **Survival barely entered the loadings before.** At α_F = 0 it does not enter at all. With
   α_F = 0.5 its median share of a loading's precision is under 1%, and α_F = 0.5 reproduces the
   April scale runaway in simulation (‖F_k‖ up to 169 times its starting value).
3. **Two errors found and fixed:**
   - the survival term of the single-modality F update left the other genes of the same program in
     the residual, so each gene re-explained the whole program and the update overshot;
   - with a signed loading prior, the SVD start discarded signs and every program collapsed.
4. **Scale canonicalization with the corrected update is stable:** every fit converges, and the
   coefficients stay bounded.
5. **Recovery is still low:** 1/20 seeds at noise 0.25 and 6/20 at noise 1, against the 80%
   threshold. This is the starting point for supervised initialization and the β prior (C3–C4).

## Test bed

Data come from the multimodal simulation's low-variance prognostic scenario, expression block only
(n = 120 training and 120 validation patients, p = 50 genes, 3 true programs). Program 3 has score
scale 0.15 and log hazard ratio 1.10; programs 1 and 2 carry the variance and are not prognostic.
Each cohort is z-standardized. A fit **recovers** the planted program when some estimated program
has absolute loading correlation ≥ 0.7 with it and a coefficient of the correct sign. A program is
**survival-active** when its posterior mean coefficient is at least 1.96 posterior SDs from zero.

The fits use a point-Laplace prior on L and F. The recommended point-exponential prior collapses
to zero programs on this centered data in 6 of 10 seeds: centered scores are signed, and a
nonnegative score prior cannot represent them.

## Diagnostics of the earlier F update (C1)

| Arm | Recovered (of 10) | Median \|cor\| with planted | Null survival-active / fit | Converged | Validation C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| α_F = 0 | 0 | 0.17 | 0.4 | 10 | 0.534 |
| α_F = 0.5 | 0 | 0.11 | 0.4 | 10 | 0.533 |
| equal weights (α_F = 0.5, precisions doubled) | 1 | 0.23 | 0.6 | 10 | 0.558 |

: C1 arms at noise 0.25 (oracle C 0.666). {#tbl-c1}

![Survival's median share of the F-update precision and $|E[\beta]|$ for the estimated program closest to the planted one, by iteration (one line per seed). Values of exactly zero are drawn at 10⁻⁶.](../figs/2026-10-15_c1_supervision_trace.png)

The diagnostics answer the four questions from the plan:

- **Is the planted direction pulled at all?** Barely. The closest program is a variance program
  whose coefficient is near 0, so survival information is gated out.
- **Survival's share now.** Median 0.7% of the loading precision at α_F = 0.5 and 14% with equal
  weights, both for programs that already carry a nonzero coefficient.
- **Does the April runaway reproduce?** Yes, at α_F = 0.5: ‖F_k‖ reaches 169 times its starting
  value.
- **Objective versus update.** The monitored objective weights survival p/(1−α)·α = 50 times
  more than genomics, while the F update weights them equally. The monitored value decreases
  32–82 times per arm across 10 fits, so it is not the objective the updates climb. The large
  survival weight also inflates the denominator of the relative-change test, so fits can stop
  early.

## Scale canonicalization and the corrected update (C2)

Each program is rescaled to unit SD of its training score after every iteration; β̃_k is then a log
hazard ratio per SD. α_F is dropped: every survival term carries one weight w_S, and w_S = 1 is the
plain posterior. The F update now removes the other genes of the program from each gene's survival
term and runs as a sequential sweep over genes, the same update the multimodal model uses. The
derivation and the correction are in `derivations/cox_on_YF/canonical_ZF/`.

| Arm | Noise | Recovered (of 20) | Null survival-active / fit | Converged | Validation C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| α_F = 0 (earlier) | 0.25 | 0 | 0.45 | 20 | 0.553 |
| canonical, w_S = 1 | 0.25 | 1 | 0.60 | 20 | 0.557 |
| α_F = 0 (earlier) | 1 | 0 | 0.15 | 20 | 0.521 |
| canonical, w_S = 1 | 1 | 6 | 0.65 | 20 | 0.641 |

: C2 arms (oracle C 0.678 at noise 0.25, 0.839 at noise 1). {#tbl-c2}

![As above for C2, by noise level.](../figs/2026-10-15_c2_supervision_trace.png)

With canonicalization the coefficients stay below 2 in absolute value, and every fit converges.
Survival's share of the loading precision rises to between 10% and 100% for the closest program at
noise 1, and the planted program is found in 6 of 20 seeds there. At noise 0.25, the variance
programs dominate the factorization and the planted program is found once.

The null survival-active rate rises by 0.15 and 0.50 per fit over α_F = 0. The second is at the
limit of the +0.5 margin.

## Supervised initialization and the β prior (C3 + C4)

Every arm uses the canonical configuration with w_S = 1. Program K starts from the null-model Cox
score direction $Y^\top u_0$, where $u_0$ are the martingale residuals of the null model. The shared
β prior is held at its starting value for 10 iterations, then refit from the K coefficients after
each sweep.

| Arm | Recovered, noise 0.25 | Recovered, noise 1 | Null survival-active / fit | Converged |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| α_F = 0 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0.45; 0.15 | 20; 20 |
| canonical (C2) | 1/20 | 6/20 | 0.60; 0.65 | 20; 20 |
| + supervised start | 1/20 | 7/20 | 0.60; 0.60 | 20; 20 |
| + shared normal prior, warm-up | 1/20 | 6/20 | 0.75; 0.60 | 20; 20 |
| + point-Laplace prior | 1/20 | 5/20 | 0.35; 0.35 | 20; 20 |
| + point-normal, slab SD 1 | 1/20 | 5/20 | 0.50; 0.40 | 10; 13 |
| fixed N(0, 2²) (reference) | 1/20 | 5/20 | 0.85; 0.70 | 20; 20 |

: C3 + C4 arms; the two values per cell are noise 0.25 and noise 1. {#tbl-c3c4}

No arm comes close to the 16/20 threshold. The supervised start correlates only 0.38 (noise 0.25)
and 0.56 (noise 1) with the planted loadings, and the program it seeds collapses in almost every
seed.

**How much can survival alone recover here?** A Cox model fit directly on the 50 genes (ridge or
lasso, cross-validated) recovers the planted direction in 0/20 or 4/20 seeds at noise 0.25, and in
4/20 or 13/20 at noise 1. The true predictor's validation C is 0.68 at noise 0.25. With 120 patients
and about 84 events, the survival data do not determine the direction well enough for 80% recovery
at the lower noise level, by this or any other method. Whether to keep this test bed, calibrate it,
or set the threshold relative to the survival-only reference is open; C5 waits on that decision.

## Calibrated test bed

The test bed was recalibrated so that the survival data identify the planted direction. The rule
was fixed in advance: the smallest training size, then the smallest planted coefficient, at which a
survival-only Cox lasso recovers the planted program in at least 18 of 20 seeds at both noise
levels. Only n = 400 with planted log hazard ratio 3.3 qualifies (lasso 18/20 and 20/20). The planted
program still explains under 0.5% of expression variance. The recovery threshold stays at 80%.

| Arm | Recovered (0.25; 1) | Null survival-active / fit | Converged | Validation C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| α_F = 0 | 1; 1 | 1.15; 0.35 | 20; 20 | 0.641; 0.540 |
| canonical, w_S = 1 (C2) | 18; 20 | 1.35; 0.35 | 20; 19 | 0.771; 0.761 |
| + supervised start | 20; 20 | 1.00; 0.30 | 20; 19 | 0.770; 0.761 |
| + shared normal β prior, warm-up | 20; 20 | 1.60; 0.65 | 20; 20 | 0.769; 0.761 |
| **+ shared point-Laplace β prior, warm-up** | **17; 19** | **1.10; 0.25** | **20; 20** | **0.763; 0.765** |
| + point-normal, slab SD 1 | 17; 19 | 1.20; 0.30 | 20; 18 | 0.763; 0.766 |
| fixed N(0, 2²) (reference) | 20; 20 | 1.70; 0.70 | 20; 20 | 0.771; 0.760 |

: Calibrated test bed (n = 400, planted log HR 3.3; oracle C 0.85 and 0.95). {#tbl-cal}

Without survival in the loadings, the planted program is missed (1/20), and validation C falls to
0.64 and 0.54. Every survival-supervised arm recovers it in most seeds and reaches validation C of
about 0.76–0.77.

The chosen configuration is the supervised start with a shared point-Laplace prior on β, which meets
every simulation criterion:
- recovery 85% and 95%;
- fewer null survival-active programs than α_F = 0;
- every fit converges;
- the most stable updates of all arms.

The normal-prior warm-up arm also passes, with higher recovery but more false positives. The
real-data check (lower 95% limit of ΔC against α_F = 0 above −0.02) comes next.

## Real data: external validation of the supervised model

The selected configuration was refitted on the reported training data (TCGA + CPTAC, K = 7) and
scored on the five external cohorts. It is compared with the reported α_F = 0 model.

| Cohort | Supervised − reported (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| Dijk | −0.050 (−0.113, 0.012) |
| Moffitt | −0.001 (−0.071, 0.065) |
| PACA-AU array | +0.010 (−0.054, 0.069) |
| PACA-AU seq | +0.029 (−0.038, 0.097) |
| Puleo | −0.002 (−0.033, 0.027) |
| **Mean of cohorts** | **−0.003 (−0.029, 0.024)** |

: External ΔC, supervised minus reported α_F = 0 model; cohort-stratified paired bootstrap. {#tbl-real-dc}

Mean external C is 0.624 for the supervised model and 0.627 for the reported one. The pre-specified
criterion, a lower 95% limit above −0.02, fails by 0.009. The point estimate is zero, and with five
cohorts the interval is about ±0.027 wide, so the criterion requires a gain of about +0.007 to pass.
The supervised model keeps three survival-active programs where the unsupervised fit keeps one.

## Multimodal model with survival supervision

The supervised start and the shared point-Laplace prior on β were carried into the multimodal model
(expression + methylation), which already had the exact loading update, the scale
canonicalization and ELBO-based pruning. Calibrated two-modality bed, starting rank 7, true rank 3:

| Arm | Recovered (0.25; 1) | Null survival-active / fit | Converged | Programs kept | Validation C |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| framework of 10/1 | 17; 16 | 0.75; 0.65 | 40/40 | 3 | 0.826; 0.892 |
| + survival supervision | **18; 20** | **0.55; 0.15** | **40/40** | **3** | **0.844; 0.943** |

: Multimodal model on the calibrated bed (20 seeds per noise level). {#tbl-mm-sup}

With supervision, the multimodal model recovers the planted program in 90% and 100% of datasets,
keeps exactly the three true programs (two that explain the variance and one that explains
survival), and has fewer false prognostic programs.

## Open: single-modality convergence and the choice of number of programs

- After an error in the monitored objective was fixed, the selected single-modality configuration
  converges in 19 of 20 fits at each noise level. The two exceptions oscillate stably
  (relative size 10⁻⁴) and still recover the planted program.
- Pruning by the ELBO, which works in the multimodal model, removes the planted program in single
  modality, where survival gains too little to offset the program's cost.

The rule for the number of programs is the next decision.

## Protected pruning and starting rank

The protected-pruning adoption assessment could not be completed as specified: the multimodal
fitter's convergence flag refers to reconstruction/predictor changes, whereas the fixed rule
requires ELBO convergence for every fit. The panel was stopped before a complete rank batch;
there is no completed result table. Protected pruning was not adopted for either model, and the
conditional real-data 1-SE run was not performed. Starting K remains 7 with the handoff
configurations. The exact protection inequality also protects a zero coefficient with zero
variance; that boundary was implemented literally, without tuning. See DECISIONS.md.

The opt-in implementation and fixed runners are retained on `m5/k-selection` for review.
The default-fit comparisons against `feature/supervised-F` preserve the full fitted objects
and pruning sequences.
